Predictions of an XAddiVortes fit

Source: R/xaddivortes.R
predict.xaddivortes.Rd

The prediction is the sum of the fitted cell values. The prediction interval is the prediction plus and minus the normal quantile times sigma(object), the fit's noise estimate: a rough interval that takes the fit as known, not a posterior interval (see xaddivortes() for calibrated intervals).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'xaddivortes'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  interval = c("none", "prediction"),
  level = 0.95,
  threads = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An object of class "xaddivortes".

newdata

New covariates, as for predict.thiessen(); NULL predicts at the training rows.

interval

"none" or "prediction".

level

The interval level, in (0, 1).

threads

Threads for this prediction; NULL takes the fit's.

...

Not used; must be empty.

Value

A numeric vector, or with an interval a matrix with columns fit, lower and upper.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # core_experimental()
set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(runif(400), ncol = 2)
y <- sin(6 * x[, 1]) + x[, 2] + rnorm(200, sd = 0.1)
fit <- xaddivortes(x, y, params = xaddivortes_params(rounds = 10),
                   control = thiessen_control(tessellations = 20),
                   seed = 1)
head(predict(fit, x))
head(predict(fit, x, interval = "prediction"))
}
